value: mites hide in cracks and crevices of the coop by day and feed on birds at night
mites can survive up to 10 months in an empty hen house and infest new birds
can be carried in on wild birds such as pigeons and sparrows
irritation and pain around the breast and legs
scabs, dark skin patches and feather loss
pale comb and wattle from anemia in heavy infestations

diagnosis.value: suspected from falling egg production, anemia and deaths in young or sick birds, confirmed by finding mites, eggs or their droppings

value: heating the henhouse above 55°C between flocks
treating walls and floors with silica dust before new hens move in

treatment_overview.value: mite-killing treatments rotated to avoid resistance, plus some newer products given orally through the drinking water; predatory mites and plant oil repellents are also used as non-chemical controls

when_to_call_vet.value: Call a vet if hens show pale combs, scabbing or a sudden drop in egg-laying, since heavy red mite infestations can cause serious anemia.

summary.value: The poultry red mite is a tiny blood-feeding parasite that hides in coop cracks by day and attacks chickens at night, causing irritation, feather loss and falling egg output. Heavy infestations can cause anemia in hens and can also bite the humans who handle the birds.
